lines.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Javier.
Thank you both for telling the truth instead of sending me back out into the rain.
Sleep well, sir. Breakfast starts downstairs at seven thirty.
See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Indicates position or movement downward.

examples.trans: The kitchen is downstairs.

examples.text: Te espero abajo en el patio.
examples.trans: I will wait for you downstairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: In en absoluto, means 'not at all'.

examples.trans: There is complete silence here.
It does not bother me at all.

meanings.note: ¡Qué alivio! means 'What a relief!'.

examples.text: El alivio es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The relief is very important here.
We talk about the relief.

meanings.note: Describes roomy bedrooms or courtyards.

examples.trans: It is a spacious piece.

examples.text: ¡En absoluto! Y este escritorio amplio bajo la ventana es ideal para mi trabajo.
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Tener ... años expresses age; hace ... años means '... years ago'.

examples.trans: The year is here.

examples.text: Vemos los años desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the years from the door.

bajar.gloss: to go down; to bring down; to lower

meanings.en: to go down; to bring down; to lower
meanings.note: Works both intransitively (go downstairs) and transitively (bring down).

examples.text: Bajo a la cocina a preparar té.
examples.trans: I go down to the kitchen to make tea.

examples.text: Bajamos las maletas por la escalera.
examples.trans: We bring the suitcases down the stairs.

meanings.note: Bajo llave means 'under lock and key'; as an adjective (bajo/baja), means 'low' or 'ground' (planta baja).

examples.trans: We sit under the lemon tree.
Keep the box under lock and key.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Dolor de cabeza means 'headache'.

examples.trans: The head is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cabezas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the heads from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Standard word in Spain for an automobile.

examples.trans: The car is here.

examples.text: Vemos los coches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cars from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.
We talk about the care.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?
Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue in present: duermo; o -> u in preterite 3rd: durmió).

examples.trans: I sleep eight hours every night.
Last night I slept wonderfully here.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: empiezo); empezar a + infinitive.

examples.text: Empiezo el turno a las siete.
examples.trans: I start my shift at seven.

examples.text: La película empezó cinco minutos tarde.
examples.trans: The film started five minutes late.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Works like gustar: me encanta el té = I love tea (tea delights me).

examples.text: Me encanta el olor a pan caliente.
examples.trans: I love the smell of warm bread.

examples.text: De niño le encantaban los trenes.
examples.trans: As a boy he loved trains.

meanings.note: Por error = by mistake.

examples.trans: The mistake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los errores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the mistakes from the door.

meanings.note: Often singular (la escalera) or plural (las escaleras) for a staircase.

examples.trans: The stairs is here.

examples.text: Vemos las escaleras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the stairss from the door.

meanings.note: Writing desk in a room or study.

examples.trans: The desk is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escritorios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the desks from the door.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Open room or physical space.

examples.trans: The space is here.

examples.text: Vemos los espacios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the spaces from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Water dripping from a ceiling or roof.

examples.trans: The roof leak is here.

examples.text: Vemos las goteras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the roof leaks from the door.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Plural ideales.

examples.trans: It is an ideal piece.

examples.text: ¡En absoluto! Y este escritorio amplio bajo la ventana es ideal para mi trabajo.
examples.trans: Not at all! And this wide desk under the window is ideal for my work.

importar.gloss: to matter; to mind (importarle a alguien)

meanings.en: to matter; to mind (importarle a alguien)
meanings.note: ¿Le importa esperar? = Do you mind waiting?

examples.text: ¿Te importa abrir un poco la ventana?
examples.trans: Do you mind opening the window a little?

examples.text: No me importa esperar cinco minutos.
examples.trans: I do not mind waiting five minutes.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: It is an included piece.
with breakfast included

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Third-person singular indirect object pronoun.

examples.text: Le llevo una taza de té caliente.
examples.trans: I am bringing you/her a cup of hot tea.
Do you like the courtyard room?

meanings.note: Plural indirect object pronoun.

examples.trans: I will prepare breakfast for you all right away.
I owe you both the whole truth.

meanings.note: Fruit tree bearing lemons (el limón -> el limonero).

examples.trans: The lemon tree is here.

examples.text: Vemos los limoneros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the lemon trees from the door.

meanings.note: Versatile everyday noun for door keys, shut-off valves, and spanners.

examples.trans: The key is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llaves desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the keys from the door.

meanings.note: Bajo la lluvia = in the rain.

examples.text: La lluvia es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The rain is very important here.
We talk about the rain.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Roble macizo = solid oak.

examples.trans: It is a solid piece.

examples.text: Roble macizo, de ochenta años. Ni una sola gotera.
examples.trans: Solid oak, eighty years old. Not a single leak.

meanings.note: De madera = wooden.

examples.trans: The wood is here.

examples.text: Vemos las maderas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the woods from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday synonym of enviar.

examples.text: Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
examples.trans: I will send you a message when I arrive.

examples.text: Mi primo me mandó naranjas de Valencia.
examples.trans: My cousin sent me oranges from Valencia.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?
I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?
It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Esta casa tiene más de ochenta años.
examples.trans: This house is over eighty years old.
I counted eighty stone steps.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb (odio = I hate).

examples.text: Odio llegar tarde a una cita.
examples.trans: I hate arriving late for an appointment.

examples.text: De pequeño odiaba madrugar en invierno.
examples.trans: As a boy he hated getting up early in winter.

meanings.note: Expresses surprise or realization.

examples.trans: Oh, there is the blue door!

examples.text: Oh, perdona, no te había visto.
examples.trans: Oh, sorry, I had not seen you.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Irregular: oigo, oyes, oye, oímos, oís, oyen; ¡Oiga! / ¡Oye! gets someone's attention.

examples.trans: Can you hear me clearly on the phone?

examples.text: Acabo de oír pasos en la escalera.
examples.trans: I just heard footsteps on the stairs.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: Describes silver metal.

examples.trans: It is a silver piece.

examples.text: ¡Qué alivio! Aquí tiene su llave plateada, Javier.
examples.trans: What a relief! Here is your silver key, Javier.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.trans: The price is here.

examples.text: Vemos los precios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the prices from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Plural proporciones.

examples.trans: The proportion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las proporciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the proportions from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

quedar.gloss: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)

meanings.en: to remain / be left; to suit; to meet up (Spain); to stay (quedarse)
meanings.note: Versatile verb: quedan dos ('two left'), le queda bien ('suits you'), quedar al mediodía ('meet at noon'), quedarse ('stay').

examples.trans: Only two vacant rooms are left.

examples.text: Esa chaqueta te queda muy bien.
examples.trans: That jacket suits you very well.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Puerta de roble = oak door.

examples.text: El roble es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The oak is very important here.
We talk about the oak.

meanings.note: Opposite of callado / tranquilo.

examples.trans: It is a noisy piece.

examples.text: El hermano mayor era decidido y ruidoso, siempre corría en las escalas de música.
examples.trans: The older brother was bold and loud, always rushing through his music scales.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Takes el when talking about someone (el señor Martín), no article when addressing directly (¡Buenos días, señor!).

examples.trans: The sir is here.

examples.text: Vemos los señores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sirs from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented conjunction, distinct from accented sí ('yes').

examples.trans: Let me know if you need another blanket.

examples.text: Mira si queda leche en la nevera.
examples.trans: Check whether any milk is left in the fridge.

meanings.note: Las siete y cuarto = seven fifteen.

examples.text: La habitación siete mira al patio.
examples.trans: Room seven overlooks the courtyard.

examples.text: Desayunamos a las siete y media.
examples.trans: We have breakfast at seven thirty.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

subir.gloss: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs

meanings.en: to go up; to climb; to carry upstairs
meanings.note: Works both intransitively and transitively.

examples.text: Subo las toallas limpias a la primera planta.
examples.trans: I carry the clean towels up to the first floor.

examples.text: Subieron despacio la escalera de madera.
examples.trans: They climbed the wooden stairs slowly.

meanings.note: Indoor ceiling (distinct from outdoor tiled tejado).

examples.trans: The ceiling is here.

examples.text: Vemos los techos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceilings from the door.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.trans: The work is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trabajos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the works from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Una ventana soleada = a sunny window.

examples.trans: The window is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ventanas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the windows from the door.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Vigas de madera = wooden roof beams.

examples.trans: The ceiling beam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vigas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ceiling beams from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.
